risks.description: The approve endpoint returns 200 with status=approved (and even persisted:true) while the durable store is never written, so the API and the persisted record disagree.
risks.basis: AC-APPROVAL-001; observed failure cluster C01/C03 — state.py shows no status=approved after a 200 response

risks.description: An approval that appears to succeed does not survive a fresh re-read of the persisted store, or is clobbered by a later unrelated approval.
risks.basis: AC-APPROVAL-002 approval state survives a re-read of persisted state

risks.description: Concurrent or retried approvals of the same invoice append multiple payments/approvals, so approving more than once pays more than once.
risks.basis: Observed failure cluster C02 — payments=1 not found; extends the accepted gen-idempotent-approve situation to races/retries

risks.description: When the approval response is delayed past the client timeout, the caller cannot tell whether the effect landed and a naive retry double-applies.
risks.basis: AC-APPROVAL-001; fixture's uncertain defect models effect-landed-then-stall

risks.description: An approval submitted without an actor field is silently dropped or rejected rather than recorded durably.
risks.basis: AC-APPROVAL-001 approving records the approval durably

risks.description: A plain read (GET) of an invoice mutates or fabricates approval state in the durable store.
risks.basis: AC-APPROVAL-001 — only approving should record an approval

scenarios.title: Approve response says approved but durable store must agree
scenarios.purpose: Detect the acknowledged-but-not-persisted divergence: after a 200 approve and an in-memory GET that both say approved, the durable store file must also show approved.
scenarios.rationale: The observed failures (C01/C03) show a 200 with status=approved that never reaches the store. The only way to catch this is to compare the API's answer against a fresh read of the durable file.
scenarios.isolation_note: Uses a dedicated invoice id (W2-UI); records are additive and namespaced by id, and the store is reset on api boot, so this cannot alter another scenario's assertions. No write-capable reset command is available for cleanup.
setup: Use invoice id W2-UI which no other scenario touches
expected_observations: GET reflects approved in the running process
The durable store read via state.py shows W2-UI status=approved
forbidden_observations: state.py reports W2-UI status=pending after a 200 approve
state.py output for W2-UI is missing entirely

scenarios.title: Approval survives re-read and a later unrelated approval
scenarios.purpose: Confirm AC-APPROVAL-002: a persisted approval is still present when the store is re-read after an unrelated invoice is approved, i.e. it is not clobbered by subsequent writes.
scenarios.rationale: gen-persist-approve only reads immediately after one approval. AC-002 is specifically about surviving a re-read; a whole-file write for a second invoice is a realistic way to accidentally lose the first record.
scenarios.isolation_note: Uses dedicated invoice ids W2-KEEP-A and W2-KEEP-B; additive per-id records and boot-time store reset mean no contamination of other scenarios. No cleanup command exists.
setup: Use invoice ids W2-KEEP-A and W2-KEEP-B
expected_observations: The first invoice's approval is present on the first re-read
After approving a second, unrelated invoice, re-reading the first still shows exactly one durable approval
forbidden_observations: W2-KEEP-A reverts to status=pending after W2-KEEP-B is approved
W2-KEEP-A approvals or payments count changes after an unrelated write

scenarios.title: Two simultaneous approvals of one invoice pay exactly once
scenarios.purpose: Exercise the race version of idempotency: two approvals issued at the same instant must leave exactly one durable approval and one payment.
scenarios.rationale: gen-idempotent-approve is sequential. A concurrency race can slip past a naive existing-approval check and double-append, so the durable count is the oracle.
scenarios.isolation_note: Uses dedicated invoice id W2-RACE; per-id additive records and boot reset prevent cross-scenario contamination. isolation_key serializes this against other store-writing scenarios so state.py never reads a half-written file. No cleanup command available.
expected_observations: Durable store shows W2-RACE approved with exactly one approval and one payment
forbidden_observations: state.py shows payments=2 or approvals=2 for W2-RACE

scenarios.title: Delayed approval lands durably and a retry does not double-pay
scenarios.purpose: Cover the ambiguous-outcome path: even if the approve response is delayed, the effect must be inspectable in the durable store and a client retry must remain idempotent.
scenarios.rationale: The fixture models an effect that lands then stalls; a caller that times out will retry. The durable store must let the caller reconcile (approved, one payment) rather than double-applying. A generous timeout keeps correct/fast code passing while still catching double-pay and non-persistence.
scenarios.isolation_note: Uses dedicated invoice id W2-AMBIG; additive per-id records and boot reset prevent contamination. No cleanup command exists.
expected_observations: After the first (possibly delayed) approve, the durable store shows the effect landed
After a retry, the store still shows exactly one payment
forbidden_observations: state.py shows W2-AMBIG status=pending after the approve returns
state.py shows payments=2 after the retry

scenarios.title: Approval with no actor is still recorded durably
scenarios.purpose: Verify a well-formed approve request that omits the actor field still produces a durable approval rather than being dropped.
scenarios.rationale: Missing optional fields are a common cause of silently skipped writes; the durable record is the only trustworthy check.
scenarios.isolation_note: Uses dedicated invoice id W2-NOACTOR; additive per-id records and boot reset prevent contamination. No cleanup command available.
expected_observations: Durable store shows W2-NOACTOR approved with one recorded approval despite the missing actor
forbidden_observations: state.py shows W2-NOACTOR status=pending after a 200 approve

scenarios.title: Reading an invoice never records an approval
scenarios.purpose: Safety invariant: a GET on an untouched invoice must leave it pending in the durable store; reads must not fabricate approvals.
scenarios.rationale: AC-001 ties recording an approval to the approve action; a read path that marks anything approved would silently create payments. Cheap to assert and high consequence.
scenarios.isolation_note: Uses dedicated invoice id W2-READONLY and only reads it; per-id additive records and boot reset prevent contamination. No cleanup command needed.
setup: Use invoice id W2-READONLY, never approved by any scenario
expected_observations: Durable store shows W2-READONLY status=pending with no approvals or payments
forbidden_observations: state.py shows W2-READONLY status=approved after only a GET

assumptions: state.py is the durable oracle: it reads store.json (not the running process) and accepts an invoice-id argument to filter output to one record (extra argument is permitted by the approved-command rule).
Invoices are created on first touch, so assigning each scenario a unique invoice id gives per-scenario isolation without a reset command.

The api service serializes writes under a lock and rewrites the whole store file non-atomically, so store-writing scenarios share isolation_key r5-fixture-store to avoid a state.py read racing a partial write.
POST /api/invoices/{id}/approve and GET /api/invoices/{id} return 200 in both correct and buggy builds; the pass/fail signal therefore comes from the durable state_check, not the HTTP status.
unresolved_questions: The fixture deletes and reseeds store.json on every api boot, so a genuine restart_recovery / crash_mid_workflow durability test would report 'pending' even for correct code. Is process-restart durability in scope for AC-APPROVAL-002, or does 'survives a re-read of persisted state' mean only a fresh-process read of the file (which state.py already does)? I did not author restart scenarios to avoid guaranteed false positives.

The endpoint has no authentication, authorization, or tenant concept, and the ACs promise none, so I did not invent authorization/cross_tenant scenarios. Confirm whether approvals must be restricted to authorized actors.

Idempotency ('pays once') is exercised by the accepted gen-idempotent-approve scenario and by my concurrency/retry scenarios, but it is not stated in AC-APPROVAL-001/002. Confirm idempotency is a hard requirement so these findings are actionable.

No approved command can reset or mutate store.json (state.py is read-only), so isolation relies entirely on per-invoice-id namespacing; confirm this is acceptable or provide a reset command for cleanup.
